title: Atomic model swap with traffic-quorum gating and reproducible rollback playback
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Production rollouts at Redwood increasingly need deterministic rollback behavior plus a low-latency fast-fail safety gate that operates across heterogeneous cohorts. This PR implements an atomic swap rollout primitive driven by a traffic-quorum policy and pairs it with a compact reproducible playback (repro-playback) artifact to warm caches and recreate in-flight behavior at rollback time. Design summary: 1) Traffic-quorum router: a policy layer that requires a configurable quorum of cohort acceptance signals before the swap is committed cluster-wide. Cohort signals are aggregated from per-route SLO checks (latency, p50/p95, error-rate, and a lightweight quality delta if available). 2) Swap transaction: swaps are executed as a two-phase transaction: prepare (shadow swap + quorum voting), then commit (atomic swap). If quorum is not met within the window, the prepare is aborted and traffic remains on the incumbent model. 3) Repro-playback artifact: during the prepare phase we capture a bounded deterministic sample (request fingerprints, prefix KV snapshots, and tokenization deltas) into a compressed playback bundle stored in the replay-store. On abort or post-commit rollback, the playback is run against the previous model/component in an isolated sandbox to validate behavior and to warm KV caches deterministically. 4) Metrics gating and backoff: the quorum evaluator supports weighted voting by cohort size and a backoff policy that escalates to traffic-splitting if partial acceptance is observed. 5) Operator UX and safety: exposes a single CLI for initiating atomic swaps with flags for quorum size, sample window, and repro-playback retention. Also adds detailed events to the rollout journal for audit and postmortem. What changed (files): controller/atomic_swap.go orchestration/quorum_router.go orchestration/quorum_evaluator_test.go replay/replay_store.go replay/replay_serializer.go cli/swapctl.go telemetry/rollout_journal.proto docs/runbooks/atomic-swap.md examples/atomic-swap-example.yaml CI/workflows/atomic-swap.yml High level commits: - feat(atomic-swap): add two-phase swap controller and quorum router - perf(replay): compact binary serializer for playback bundles - test(quorum): add end-to-end acceptance tests with synthetic cohorts - docs: runbook and example usage - ci: workflow and end-to-end smoke job Review summary: Initial review requested on 2026-02-17. Liam: requested stronger invariants on the prepare abort path and clearer eventing for audit logs (addressed: added explicit prepare-abort event and idempotent cleanup). Maya: flagged potential N+1 metric queries in the quorum evaluator (addressed: added aggregate metric snapshotting and cache). Chen: asked for staged rollout path if quorum partially passes; implemented weighted-split fallback with operator opt-in. CI: The first CI run showed a flaky integration test in orchestration/quorum_evaluator_test.go due to time-dependent sampling; fixed by introducing deterministic clock in tests. Final CI: all checks green. Testing and canary plan: - unit/integration coverage added for quorum lifetime, abort/commit paths, and repro-playback execution. - End-to-end smoke on staging with two synthetic cohorts (region-us / region-eu) and production-like load. - Canary: initial usage gated to 5% traffic with manual approval for 25% then 100% after 24h and automatic rollback on failed quorum windows. Migration notes and compatibility: - No data-format changes to persisted models. Replay bundle storage is compatible with existing replay-store but uses a new serializer version; migration path included to rehydrate older bundles. - Operators should review default quorum (set to 0.6 weighted) and sampling window (default 120s) in the rollout config. Rollback semantics: - Abort during prepare leaves incumbent untouched and deletes ephemeral bundles older than retention threshold. - Post-commit rollback triggers repro-playback to warm former model and validate behavior before switching live traffic back. Audit trail: All prepare/commit/abort/rollback events are written to telemetry/rollout_journal.proto and surfaced in Console under the rollout activity tab. Security and perf considerations: - Bundles are encrypted at rest using cluster KMS keys and access-controlled. - Repro-playback runs are throttled to avoid spike load; KV cache warmup uses controlled prefix-inserts. Runbook and docs: added docs/runbooks/atomic-swap.md with step-by-step operator guidance, escalation playbook, and CLI examples. Linear/JIRA references: ENG-9123 covers the core runtime changes; PM-204 tracks the UX and rollout defaults. Checklist: [ ] Add canary to staging and validate metrics [x] Add deterministic-clock to tests [x] Add event journaling for audit [x] Add CLI and example [x] Secure bundle storage [x] CI passing Merge outcome and rationale: Given green tests, addressed reviewer changes, and an explicit staging canary plan, this PR was merged via squash-merge to main on 2026-02-24. The feature enables safer, auditable atomic swaps with deterministic rollback behavior and reproducible cache warmup which reduces rollback flakiness in production.
